nodes.description: Move the artifact format checks into the deterministic validator so that title, front matter, chapter numerals, summary length, keyword count, double spacing, page numbering, citation numbering, and forbidden names are all re-derived from the artifact bytes on every run, and prove the gate fires by mutating the artifact.
nodes.question: The builder asserts the official format. What prevents a later rebuild from silently losing it?
alternatives: trust the builder
check the artifact by hand after each build
move the checks into the deterministic gate and prove they fail closed
nodes.falsifier: If a mutated artifact passes the gate, the check is decorative and must be rewritten.

nodes.description: Deterministic gate that re-derives the submission artifact format from its own bytes; five mutations were shown to fail it and restoration returns to pass.

nodes.title: Reproducibility is Not Enough: Artifact Verifiability in Decentralized-Build Package Ecosystems

nodes.description: Make the build deterministic by pinning every packed entry timestamp and the document property timestamps to the epoch already used for the deterministic PDF, and write parts in sorted order. Keep the builder committed so the instructions travel with the artifact.
nodes.question: Must the submission artifact be byte-reproducible, or is a correct-looking rebuild enough?
alternatives: accept content equivalence and stop pinning the artifact digest
pin the digest and rebuild only on one machine
make the build deterministic so any checkout reproduces the same bytes
nodes.falsifier: If two checkouts at the same commit produce different digests, the build is still not reproducible and the receipt cannot be trusted.

nodes.description: Submission artifact made byte-reproducible: a clean-clone rebuild at the same commit now yields an identical digest, verified after diagnosing zip and document-property timestamps.

nodes.description: Measure the decision record with a committed script and fixtures, and report that 3 of 27 recorded decisions were revised, every revision triggered by the project's own executed measurement, alongside the explicit statement that a single project without a comparison group cannot show the practice caused the revisions.
nodes.question: The thesis claims the loop corrects itself. What is the measured value of that claim?
alternatives: assert self-correction narratively
count only the falsified endpoint
census the whole decision record with committed code and report the rate with its limits
nodes.falsifier: If the census counts records the ledger does not contain, or misses revised decisions, the number is wrong and the claim must be withdrawn.

nodes.description: Committed census of the project decision record: 28 records, 15 groups, all with falsifiers, 3 revised, every revision triggered by the project own executed measurement; descriptive only, no comparison group.
Validation gate that rebuilds the submission artifact from its committed builder and fails when the digest differs from the committed artifact; proven by tampering.

Blinded 25-item calibration form completed at the intended 10/10/5 confidence stratification, machine-checked for leakage and field uniformity; no labels collected, so judged scoring stays inadmissible.

nodes.question: What cost quantity should the confirmatory block report per episode?
alternatives: wall-clock duration as a proxy
total tokens reported by the provider
dollar cost
marginal input plus output tokens with the fixed floor reported separately
nodes.falsifier: If the fixed floor varies materially across episodes of the same backend, treating it as a constant is wrong and cost must be modelled per episode.

nodes.description: Per-episode cost measured from the structured usage stream: a fixed 46,763-token context floor identical across probes, and a 12.03x dollar-cost difference for identical work driven by cache state rather than by condition.

nodes.description: Report context tokens and marginal tokens as two separate quantities per episode, treat neither as constant, and continue to exclude dollar cost from comparisons because it still varies with cache state.
nodes.question: After the fixed-floor assumption failed on real episodes, what cost quantity is admissible?
alternatives: keep marginal tokens and a constant floor
report only total tokens
report context tokens and marginal tokens as two separate quantities
nodes.falsifier: If context tokens for the same condition and task vary widely across repeats, a per-episode report is still not enough and cost must be modelled with repeats.

nodes.description: Replication of the cost instrument on real episodes: the probe-measured fixed floor failed, context tokens differed by 24,900 between conditions and totals by a factor of 1.487, firing the previous decision falsifier.

nodes.role: run-variance evidence, reviewed but not cited in the manuscript

nodes.description: Report every cost quantity as a mean over repeats with its observed spread, never as a single episode, and treat the retrieval condition as requiring more repeats than the minimal condition because its variance is roughly four times larger.
nodes.question: Is a single episode enough to report the cost of a condition?
alternatives: report one episode per condition
report repeats only for the retrieval condition
report every cost quantity as a mean over repeats with its spread, and never as a single episode
nodes.falsifier: If the spread of the retrieval condition does not shrink as repeats increase, the variance is not sampling noise but a property of the condition, and cost must be modelled as a distribution rather than summarised by a mean.

nodes.description: Three repeats per condition on one burned task: minimal condition context varied 2.90 percent, retrieval condition 11.34 percent, with the retrieval range covering 61.1 percent of the between-condition gap.

Void every cost number the instrument produced across the three preceding cycles, sum usage over completed calls, write transcripts to files and report whether each is complete, and re-measure all six episodes before any cost figure is used again.
nodes.question: The cost instrument was wrong by an order of magnitude and its fixture protected the error. What must change?
alternatives: patch the parser and keep the reported numbers
patch the parser and re-run only the affected condition
void every number the instrument produced, fix the parser, capture complete transcripts, and re-measure from scratch
nodes.falsifier: If a transcript reports complete but its summed call count disagrees with the provider billing record, the aggregation is still wrong.

nodes.description: Instrument defect: the cost parser read the last usage record as the run total, understating one episode 14.4-fold, and its fixture encoded the same wrong assumption. Two further defects, transcript truncation and buffer swallowing, surfaced during repair.
Corrected cost over six episodes from complete transcripts: minimal condition 167,251 total tokens over 3.3 calls, full condition 520,969 over 9.7 calls, with no factor attribution.

add more assertions where they look thin

nodes.description: Paired suites written for the three previously unaudited instrument modules; 21 further mutations injected, 20 caught, 1 shown by execution to be an equivalent mutant. No instrument module now lacks a suite.

re-run the blocks from scratch

nodes.description: Deterministic results of both executed blocks re-derived from retained artifacts with the audited instruments and matching exactly; judged verdicts excluded as nondeterministic; an independent canary scan found no leak.
